You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 7a58b8d6021426b796eebfae80983374d9a80a75 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Date: Sun, 18 Sep 2022 11:33:12 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] usb: chipidea: fix deadlock in ci_otg_del_timer

There is a deadlock in ci_otg_del_timer(), the process is
shown below:

    (thread 1)                  |        (thread 2)
ci_otg_del_timer()              | ci_otg_hrtimer_func()
  ...                           |
  spin_lock_irqsave() //(1)     |  ...
  ...                           |
  hrtimer_cancel()              |  spin_lock_irqsave() //(2)
  (block forever)

We hold ci->lock in position (1) and use hrtimer_cancel() to
wait ci_otg_hrtimer_func() to stop, but ci_otg_hrtimer_func()
also need ci->lock in position (2). As a result, the
hrtimer_cancel() in ci_otg_del_timer() will be blocked forever.

This patch extracts hrtimer_cancel() from the protection of
spin_lock_irqsave() in order that the ci_otg_hrtimer_func()
could obtain the ci->lock.

What`s more, there will be no race happen. Because the
"next_timer" is always under the protection of
spin_lock_irqsave() and we only check whether "next_timer"
equals to NUM_OTG_FSM_TIMERS in the following code.

Fixes: 3a316ec4c91c ("usb: chipidea: use hrtimer for otg fsm timers")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220918033312.94348-1-duoming@zju.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c b/drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c
index ada78daba6df..c17516c29b63 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c
@@ -256,8 +256,10 @@ static void ci_otg_del_timer(struct ci_hdrc *ci, enum otg_fsm_timer t)
 	ci->enabled_otg_timer_bits &= ~(1 << t);
 	if (ci->next_otg_timer == t) {
 		if (ci->enabled_otg_timer_bits == 0) {
+			spin_unlock_irqrestore(&ci->lock, flags);
 			/* No enabled timers after delete it */
 			hrtimer_cancel(&ci->otg_fsm_hrtimer);
+			spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags);
 			ci->next_otg_timer = NUM_OTG_FSM_TIMERS;
 		} else {
 			/* Find the next timer */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c`**
- The function `ci_otg_del_timer` was modified to change the order of operations regarding the locking mechanism.
- Specifically, the `hrtimer_cancel(&ci->otg_fsm_hrtimer);` call was moved outside of the `spin_lock_irqsave()` protection. 
- The sequence now first unlocks the spinlock before calling `hrtimer_cancel()`, and then re-locks it afterward. This change prevents a deadlock situation that could occur when `ci_otg_hrtimer_func()` tries to acquire the same lock while `hrtimer_cancel()` is waiting for it to release.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification addresses a deadlock issue that arises from two threads trying to acquire the same lock in a conflicting manner. By restructuring the locking around the `hrtimer_cancel()` call, the patch ensures that the timer can be canceled without blocking the thread that needs to acquire the lock for further operations.
- The change maintains the integrity of the timer management by ensuring that the check for `next_timer` still occurs under the protection of the lock, thus preventing any race conditions while allowing the timer cancellation to proceed without deadlock.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags); // (1)
hrtimer_cancel(&ci->otg_fsm_hrtimer); // (2)
spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags); // (3)
```
Reason:
The deadlock occurs because `ci_otg_del_timer()` holds the lock (`ci->lock`) while calling `hrtimer_cancel()`, which in turn requires the same lock to be acquired by `ci_otg_hrtimer_func()`. This creates a situation where both threads are waiting on each other indefinitely, leading to a deadlock.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
spin_unlock_irqrestore(&ci->lock, flags); // (1)
hrtimer_cancel(&ci->otg_fsm_hrtimer); // (2)
spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags); // (3)
```
Reason:
The patch fixes the deadlock by unlocking `ci->lock` before calling `hrtimer_cancel()`, allowing `ci_otg_hrtimer_func()` to acquire the lock and complete its operation. This change ensures that the timer cancellation can proceed without blocking, thus preventing the deadlock situation.
